content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define diffusion and explain why it occurs
Identify the factors that affect the rate of diffusion
Describe examples of diffusion in living organisms
Explain why diffusion is important for cells

is one of the key ways that substances move into, out of, and within cells. It is a passive process, meaning it does not require energy from the cell. Understanding diffusion is essential for understanding how cells obtain nutrients and remove waste products.
is the net movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration, down a concentration gradient.
Particles move randomly in all directions
There is NET movement from high to low concentration
Continues until equilibrium is reached (concentrations equal)

attrs.alt: Particles diffusing from high to low concentration until equilibrium

content.text: All particles have kinetic energy and move randomly
Where there are more particles (higher concentration), more will move away
Where there are fewer particles (lower concentration), fewer will move away
The net result is movement from high to low concentration

content.text: is the difference in concentration between two regions.
= big difference in concentration = faster diffusion
= no gradient = no net movement (particles still move, but equally in both directions)
Factors Affecting the Rate of Diffusion
Greater difference drives more net movement
Particles have more kinetic energy, move faster
More area for particles to cross

Oxygen diffuses from alveoli into blood
CO₂ diffuses from blood into alveoli

content.text: Digested food molecules (glucose, amino acids, fatty acids) diffuse from the gut lumen into the blood through the villi.
Good blood supply removes absorbed molecules (maintains gradient)
Neurotransmitters diffuse across the synaptic gap from one neurone to the next.
Single-celled organisms like amoeba rely entirely on diffusion:
Oxygen diffuses in from the surrounding water
Their small size means short diffusion distances
Investigate the effect of concentration on rate of diffusion using agar jelly and an indicator.
Cut agar jelly (containing indicator) into equal-sized cubes
Place cubes in different concentrations of acid (or alkali)
Time how long for colour to change throughout
Investigate diffusion of potassium permanganate in water at different temperatures.
Dependent: Time for colour change (or distance diffused)
Control: Size of cubes, volume of liquid, temperature (if not being tested)

Large organisms need specialised exchange surfaces (lungs, gills, villi)
